Data science uses statistics, programming, visualization, and machine learning to understand data and support decisions. A typical workflow is collect data, clean it, analyze it, model it, and evaluate results.
Training means showing the model many examples, computing prediction error with a loss function, calculating gradients with backpropagation, and updating weights to reduce future error.
NumPy is a Python library for fast arrays, matrix multiplication, and numerical computing. In this project it stores weights, does neural-network math, and samples generated tokens.

A language model predicts the next token from previous tokens. Large language models use huge datasets and many parameters. This notebook uses a tiny character RNN, so it is only an educational miniature.

Gradients measure how changing each weight changes the loss. The optimizer uses gradients to move weights in the direction that usually improves predictions.
Loss is a number that measures how wrong the model is. Lower loss usually means the model is predicting the training examples better.
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data instead of learning patterns that work on new data. Tiny datasets make overfitting very easy.
